queries.query: the concealed mystery's exposition of the giants of Genesis: men of renown from eternity who worked wonders through the Tetragrammaton's name yet without holiness, and the divine spirit that will not abide in flesh forever
queries.note: 'There were giants in the earth' and the men of the name (ch. V on Gen. vi); 'men of the name', 'exercised themselves in the name', 'and not the holy inferiors' paraphrased away; the Gen. vi frame, work title, and corpus-native 'Tetragrammaton' kept as reader-honest anchors. First draft without title/Tetragrammaton anchors kept the tradition but missed the work in top-15.

queries.query: why the serpent that came from Moses' staff is called a shell of middle nature between the holy and the profane, springing over the hills in hundreds of leaps and gripping its own tail in its teeth
queries.note: The serpent of Nogah (ch. V); 'rod of Moses' rephrased to 'staff', 'Nogah, or splendour', 'three hundred and seventy leaps', 'he leapeth upon the mountains, and rusheth swiftly over the hills' paraphrased away or approximated; 'Moses' kept as a name any reader knows.

queries.query: how is strict judgment tempered by mercy in the divine ordering of the world
queries.note: The four kinds of judgment (rigorous, gentle, by balance, and neither); judgment-tempered-by-mercy is answered across many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.
